title: Early Tamil Pottery AI - Artifact Annotation
description: One annotation of one ARTIFACT by one annotator at one time (Milestone 7). Annotations are APPEND-ONLY: a revision is a new record that names the one it supersedes; nothing is overwritten. Several annotators may annotate the same artifact; their records coexist so disagreement can be analysed. Source metadata (data/metadata/records.jsonl) and acquisition provenance are NEVER modified by annotation. Missing information uses the sentinels 'unknown' (not determined), 'not_available' (no information to determine it from) and 'not_applicable' (the question does not apply). Enumerated categories marked 'project annotation category' are working vocabulary for annotators, not archaeological classifications established in the literature.

confidence.description: Annotator's confidence in the specific value. 'unknown' when not assessed.

signed_year.description: Signed year: negative = BCE, positive = CE, no year 0. null = bound not established.

provenance_type.description: WHO asserts the values in this record. source_information = a project annotator transcribing what a cited source says (requires references). project_annotation = the project's own annotator examining the image. expert_annotation = a qualified archaeologist/epigraphist. ai_prediction = model output; never a label.

region.description: A rectangle on one photograph, NORMALISED to that image: x, y (top-left) and width, height as fractions of the image width/height, measured on the original stored image in data/raw (EXIF orientation applied).

label.description: 'character' (schema 1.2.0) marks ONE sign / glyph inside an inscription; give sign_index (reading order, 1-based) and, if it can be read, sign_reading.

sign_index.description: Schema 1.2.0 (character regions only): position of the sign in the reading, 1-based.

sign_reading.description: Schema 1.2.0 (character regions only): the sign as read, or '?' if it cannot be read. Never guessed.

source.description: ref_id of the reference proposing it, or 'this_annotator'.

supports.description: What the observation supports, in words (e.g. 'consistent with the late forms in R1 table X').

association.description: For stratigraphy/absolute_dating: how securely the dated material is tied to THIS object (docs/CHRONOLOGICAL_SCOPE.md Position D).

source_reference.description: ref_id in this annotation's references, or 'annotator_observation'.

verification_status.description: verified_against_source = a human checked the claim in the physical publication. bibliographic_only = the work exists; the claim is not checked. unverified = neither.

image_usability.description: ARCHAEOLOGICAL usability of one photograph, judged by the annotator. Deliberately separate from the technical quality flags computed by preprocessing.

image_ids.description: Photographs of the artifact the annotator examined.

qualification.description: For experts: stated qualification and affiliation. Self-declared; recorded, not verified by software.

supersedes.description: annotation_id this record revises (same annotator, same artifact), or null.

review_state.description: unreviewed | project_reviewed | expert_reviewed | disputed. Only expert_reviewed expert annotations can ever become ground truth.

pottery_type.description: Same vocabulary as image_record.pottery_type (kept identical by a test).

object_status.description: Schema 1.1.0 (optional). Is the photographed object an original archaeological object or a modern reproduction/replica? 'uncertain' = examined, cannot tell; 'unknown' = not assessed. A reproduction is never an archaeological label (promotion rule P10).

object_notes.description: Schema 1.1.0 (optional). Basis for object_status and other object comments (e.g. museum label, catalogue, visual features).

inscription_present.description: 'uncertain' = examined, cannot tell. 'unknown' = not examined / not determined.

inscription_type.description: PROJECT ANNOTATION CATEGORY describing what the mark does, where the annotator can tell. Not an established archaeological typology.

script_type.description: Same vocabulary as image_record.script_type (kept identical by a test).

characters_visible.description: Count of distinct characters/marks visible; null = not counted.

reading.description: Reading in Tamil script or Brahmi Unicode as the annotator/source gives it; editorial conventions preserved.

reading_completeness.description: Schema 1.2.0 (optional). complete = every sign read; partial = some signs read, others lost or doubtful (mark them in the reading); fragmentary = only isolated signs; illegible = marks present but nothing can be read (no reading is given); unknown = not assessed.

interpretation_type.description: PROJECT ANNOTATION CATEGORY. 'not_translatable' = a reading exists but is not a translatable text (e.g. a sign). 'not_applicable' = there is no reading.

translation.description: English rendering, or a sentinel. A personal name takes 'not_applicable'.

meaning.description: Explanation in words, e.g. 'Proper name; no literal translation established.'

unresolved_conflict.description: Schema 1.1.0 (optional). Conflicting dating positions or evidence the annotator could not resolve. Recorded, never averaged.

adjudication.description: Schema 1.2.0 (optional). This record is an EXPERT ADJUDICATION: having read the listed annotations of the same artifact (which disagree), the adjudicator records their own decision in this record's fields. The listed annotations are not changed and stay visible. Rule N18.

resolves.description: annotation_ids of the current human annotations considered (at least two).

outcome.description: decided = the adjudicator stands by the values in this record; insufficient_evidence = the photograph(s) cannot settle it (script_type must then be 'uncertain' or 'unknown').

basis.description: Why: what was examined and why one view was preferred.
